title: The light in the sun
hook: Krishna says the light in sun, fire and every body is his; why Hindus chant before meals
carry: the divine light is seated in every heart

segments.voice: Yesterday, ashvattha: the world of change as an upside-down fig, cut with the axe of not clinging. Today, light.

The power goes out at night. The fridge goes quiet, the screen goes black. Someone finds a candle and strikes a match, and a small flame fills the room. Outside, the moon is lighting the street. And the whole time, without anyone noticing, a body keeps its own quiet warmth, turning the day's food into heat. Light in the sky, light in the flame, warmth inside a person: a chain of light and heat. Chapter fifteen walks down that exact chain, and at every link Krishna says the same thing: that's me.
screen: `A CANDLE IN THE DARK.` → `THE MOON OVER THE STREET.` → `WARMTH INSIDE A PERSON.`

segments.voice: Still in the chariot, the two armies waiting, Krishna keeps teaching Arjuna. It starts with you. Verse seven: a fragment of me, eternal, became the living being in the world of life. Mamaivamsha: a part of my own self. Verse eight gives a gentle picture: when that living self takes a body and leaves it, it carries the senses along, the way the wind carries scent from a flower. You can't see it go, but something has moved. Then the chain of light. Verse twelve: the brightness in the sun that lights the whole world, the light in the moon, the light in fire: know that light as mine. Verse thirteen: entering the earth, I hold up all beings with my energy; becoming the juicy moon, soma, I nourish the plants. Verse fourteen: becoming the fire of digestion in living bodies, joined with the breath going in and out, I digest the four kinds of food. So in this chapter, the divine isn't only far off. Krishna says he is the warmth in the belly after dinner. Verse fifteen brings it all the way home: I am seated in the heart of all. From me come memory, knowledge, and their loss. Here is the teaching, plainly: for Hindus, God isn't only far above the world. God lives inside every being, the antaryami, the one within. And it's why so many Hindus, before eating, chant verse fourteen: aham vaishvanaro bhutva, I am the fire in living bodies. Dinner becomes an offering to the one already inside you.
screen: `A FRAGMENT OF ME, IN YOU.` · `LIGHT IN SUN, MOON AND FIRE.` · `THE FIRE THAT DIGESTS YOUR FOOD.` · `SEATED IN THE HEART OF ALL.` · then, large: `THE LIGHT IN THE SUN.`

segments.voice: Before your next meal, try what many Hindu families do: pause and offer it, silently or with the words aham vaishvanaro. If you don't pray, feel the warmth in your hands and belly and follow it back to the sun. Then rest at the center of your chest, where verse fifteen says the light is seated.
Tejas, brilliance, radiance. Gita fifteen, twelve: the brightness in the sun, the moon and the fire is Krishna's light; verse fifteen says that light is seated in every heart.
Your line: the divine light is seated in every heart. Krishna's words: sun, moon, fire, and the fire in you. See you at day two hundred twelve.

howItsDone: Many Hindus chant Gita 15.14, 'aham vaishvanaro bhutva', before meals, often after 4.24, 'brahmarpanam'; some families and communities recite the whole of chapter fifteen before eating.

options: wind carrying scent from a flower.
fork.reveal: wind carrying scent. you can't see the scent move, but it's gone from one place and present in another.

original.note: Sanskrit: tejas, brilliance, radiance; the brightness in the sun that Krishna calls his own in Gita 15.12.

what a scholar hears: 15.12–15.15 move from cosmic light to vaishvanara, the digestive fire joined with prana and apana, to the heart; 15.7 calls the living being 'mamaivamsha', a part of me.

Krishna.meaning: God as Arjuna's charioteer and teacher in the Gita

antaryami.meaning: the one within: God dwelling inside every being

aham vaishvanaro bhutva.meaning: 'I, becoming the fire in living bodies': Gita 15.14, chanted before meals

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 15.7–15.11 (a fragment of me; the self carries the senses like wind carries scent)

Bhagavad Gita 15.15 (seated in the heart of all)

notes: howItsDone says some families recite chapter 15 before meals: a known custom in some communities (e.g., parts of South India, ISKCON), but confirm phrasing.
Original word is tejas (15.12: yad aditya-gatam tejo); confirm spelling and pronunciation.
The carry 'I am the light' is framed explicitly as Krishna's words, so it doesn't read as the listener claiming divinity.
